title: Multi-Stage Builds
summary: Multi-stage builds allow using multiple FROM instructions in a single Dockerfile. Each stage begins a fresh image and can selectively copy artifacts from earlier builder stages using COPY --from=stage.
best_practices: Use early stages for build toolchains and compilers
Copy only compiled binaries or isolated virtualenvs into the final runtime stage
Name build stages with AS <name> for readability
Leverage BuildKit parallel DAG execution
common_mistakes: Leaving build SDKs (gcc, make) in the final production runtime
Failing to name stages leading to brittle numeric indices

title: CMD vs ENTRYPOINT Instructions
summary: ENTRYPOINT specifies the permanent executable a container runs, while CMD specifies default arguments that can be overridden at runtime. Always use the exec form (JSON array) rather than shell form.
best_practices: Use exec form JSON array: ENTRYPOINT ["executable", "param1"]
Use CMD to provide sensible overridable defaults
Ensure PID 1 receives POSIX signals (SIGTERM) for graceful container shutdown
common_mistakes: Using shell form which wraps command in /bin/sh -c and prevents signal propagation
Confusing overridability of CMD with ENTRYPOINT

title: Compose Specification and Obsolete Version Key
summary: Under the modern Compose Specification (compose.yaml), the top-level version: attribute is obsolete and ignored by Compose V2. Filename conventions prefer compose.yaml.
best_practices: Name files compose.yaml or compose.yml
Omit the top-level version: attribute entirely
Use modern 'docker compose' CLI command instead of legacy python 'docker-compose'
common_mistakes: Retaining obsolete version: '3.8' which produces deprecation warnings
Using legacy docker-compose v1 CLI tool

title: Python & FastAPI Dockerfile Optimization
summary: Optimizing Python Dockerfiles requires layer reordering (copy requirements.txt before source code), selecting slim base images, using BuildKit cache mounts for pip, and enforcing non-root execution.
best_practices: Use python:3.12-slim-bookworm instead of full bloated python:3.12 base
Copy dependency manifests first to maximize Docker layer cache hits
Use --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip with BuildKit
Create and switch to non-root user (USER 10001:10001)
common_mistakes: COPY . . before pip install, breaking layer cache on every code change
Running containers as root (UID 0)
Leaving apt package lists and pip cache in image layers

title: Storage Mount Types: Bind, Volume, tmpfs
summary: Docker supports three storage types: bind mounts (host filesystem paths, ideal for dev live reload), named volumes (managed storage in /var/lib/docker/volumes/, best for databases), and tmpfs (in-memory, ideal for secrets).
best_practices: Use named volumes for persistent production database state
Use bind mounts for local development source code mounting
Use tmpfs mounts for ephemeral sensitive credentials
common_mistakes: Using bind mounts for production databases across differing host OS filesystems
Storing state in container writable layers leading to disk bloat and data loss

title: Container Exit Codes and Restart Forensics
summary: When a container restarts unexpectedly, docker inspect --format='{{json .State}}' reveals the exit code. Exit Code 137 indicates SIGKILL (often Linux kernel OOMKilled), Exit 143 indicates SIGTERM, and healthcheck failures trigger restart policies.
best_practices: Inspect container State.OOMKilled boolean via docker inspect
Review host kernel ring buffer with dmesg -T | grep -i oom
Configure memory reservation and resource limits in compose.yaml
common_mistakes: Assuming application crashed when it was actually killed by host kernel OOM killer
Missing restart policy loops caused by failing healthchecks

title: Deprecated Instructions: MAINTAINER
summary: The MAINTAINER instruction is deprecated in favor of LABEL maintainer='...'. Labels provide generic key-value metadata that can be queried and indexed cleanly.
best_practices: Use LABEL maintainer="Your Name <email@example.com>"
Use standard OCI image annotations: LABEL org.opencontainers.image.authors="..."
common_mistakes: Continuing to use obsolete MAINTAINER instruction which triggers linter errors

title: BuildKit Cache Mounts for Package Managers
summary: BuildKit syntax frontend allows mounting persistent cache directories during build execution using RUN --mount=type=cache,target=.... This preserves package manager downloads across builds without bloating layers.
best_practices: Include # syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7 at top of Dockerfile
Mount /root/.cache/pip for Python pip installations
Mount /var/cache/apt and /var/lib/apt for apt-get package installs
common_mistakes: Using standard RUN without cache mounts forcing repeated wheel downloads over internet

title: Non-Root User Container Execution
summary: Running container processes as root (UID 0) presents critical privilege escalation hazards if a container breakout occurs. Always create an unprivileged user and declare USER <uid>:<gid>.
best_practices: Create system user with explicit high UID/GID (e.g. groupadd -g 10001 app && useradd -u 10001 -g app app)
Switch to USER 10001:10001 before ENTRYPOINT or CMD
Use COPY --chown=10001:10001 to assign file ownership
common_mistakes: Omitting USER instruction leaving container running as root (Hadolint DL3002)
Using chown in a separate RUN layer which duplicates files and doubles image size

title: Base Image Selection: Slim vs Alpine vs Distroless
summary: Choosing the right base image balances size, compatibility, and security. Debian slim images (-slim-bookworm) offer glibc compatibility, Alpine uses musl libc, and Distroless eliminates shells and package managers entirely.
best_practices: Use python:3.12-slim-bookworm for standard Python projects to avoid musl C-extension build issues
Use gcr.io/distroless/static for statically compiled Go or Rust binaries
Pin explicit image tags rather than using latest
common_mistakes: Using default full distribution base images which add 800+ MB of unnecessary tools
Using :latest tag which causes non-deterministic builds

title: .dockerignore Syntax and Build Context Optimization
summary: The .dockerignore file excludes files and directories from the Docker build context. This prevents sending unnecessary git histories, virtual environments, local secrets, and caches to the Docker daemon.
best_practices: Always include .git, .env, .venv, and node_modules in .dockerignore
Keep the build context minimal to speed up initial transfer times
Use wildcards and negation patterns (!file) to strictly allow only required artifacts
common_mistakes: Missing .dockerignore resulting in multi-gigabyte build context uploads
Accidentally leaking production .env files into image layers

title: Hadolint DL3008: Pin apt-get Package Versions
summary: Hadolint rule DL3008 advises pinning versions in apt-get install and always passing --no-install-recommends. This prevents uncontrolled upstream upgrades and prevents installing hundreds of megabytes of documentation.
best_practices: Pass --no-install-recommends to apt-get install
Combine apt-get update && apt-get install in the same RUN layer
Pin critical package versions where deterministic reproducibility is required
common_mistakes: Running apt-get update in a separate layer which gets cached indefinitely
Installing recommended and suggested packages unintentionally

title: Hadolint DL3009: Clean Up Apt Lists
summary: Hadolint rule DL3009 requires deleting the apt-get cache lists after installing packages. The command rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* must be executed in the exact same RUN instruction.
best_practices: Append && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* to apt-get install commands
Chain commands with backslashes in a single RUN instruction
common_mistakes: Running rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* in a subsequent RUN layer, which does not shrink previous layer

title: Hadolint DL3013 / DL3042: Avoid Pip Cache Bloat
summary: Hadolint DL3013 and DL3042 require avoiding pip cache bloat in image layers. Use pip install --no-cache-dir or BuildKit cache mounts to prevent storing tarballs inside the final image.
best_practices: Use pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
Or use BuildKit RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip
Pin dependency package versions in requirements.txt
common_mistakes: Default pip install leaving hundreds of megabytes of wheels in /root/.cache

title: Hadolint DL3020: Use COPY Instead of ADD
summary: Hadolint rule DL3020 mandates using COPY instead of ADD for copying local files and directories. ADD has implicit archive auto-extraction and remote URL fetching behaviors that can cause unexpected bugs.
best_practices: Always use COPY for local application source code and configuration files
Reserve ADD only for automatic tar archive unpacking into the image
common_mistakes: Using ADD for local directories which inflates complexity and risks unexpected decompression

title: Hadolint DL3025: JSON Exec Notation for CMD/ENTRYPOINT
summary: Hadolint DL3025 checks that CMD and ENTRYPOINT arguments use JSON array notation (["executable", "param"]). Shell form starts an unnecessary subshell and blocks POSIX signal handling.
best_practices: Declare: CMD ["uvicorn", "main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]
Avoid string shell form: CMD uvicorn main:app
common_mistakes: Using shell form resulting in containers hanging for 10 seconds before being forcefully killed (SIGKILL) on shutdown

title: Compose Specification Healthcheck Configuration
summary: Compose healthchecks declare how Docker monitors service readiness and availability. A failing healthcheck triggers dependency ordering conditions (depends_on: service_healthy).
best_practices: Define test commands using lightweight internal utilities (curl, python urllib, or wget)
Configure reasonable interval (30s), timeout (5s), and retries (3)
Set start_period to allow slow applications time to boot without failing checks
common_mistakes: Setting timeout too low resulting in false-positive container restarts
Failing to set start_period on apps with database migrations

title: Docker Buildx Multi-Platform Emulation
summary: Docker Buildx extends the Docker CLI with full BuildKit support, enabling multi-platform compilation (--platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64) using QEMU emulation or cross-compilation toolchains.
best_practices: Create a dedicated buildx builder instance: docker buildx create --use
Use BuildKit multi-stage builds with TARGETARCH and BUILDARCH build arguments
Export cache using --cache-to type=gha or type=registry
common_mistakes: Building images on Apple Silicon (arm64) without targeting linux/amd64 for x86 cloud deployments

title: Linux Kernel Out-Of-Memory Killer Diagnostics
summary: When a container consumes more memory than its limit, the Linux kernel invokes the OOM Killer to terminate processes. The container exits with code 137 and State.OOMKilled is set to true.
best_practices: Check dmesg -T | grep -E -i 'oom|killed process' on the host
Check docker inspect <id> --format '{{.State.OOMKilled}}'
Adjust container memory limits and profiling memory usage under load
common_mistakes: Assuming memory leaks are network disconnects because logs terminate abruptly without error tracebacks

title: Rootless Docker Engine Architecture
summary: Rootless mode allows running the Docker daemon and containers as a non-root user to mitigate potential container breakout vulnerabilities. It uses user namespaces to map container root (UID 0) to an unprivileged host UID.
best_practices: Use Rootless mode for multi-tenant and security-sensitive hosting environments
Ensure slirp4netns or rootlesskit is configured for user-mode networking
Combine rootless daemon with unprivileged USER directives inside Dockerfiles
common_mistakes: Assuming running a container as root inside rootless Docker has the same host privileges as rootful Docker
